learning: Iteration 4 (0.10 m track, kp 0.7) lost progress on the s-bend (0.156 to 0.081) and slalom while reducing oscillation, so the narrow track looks sluggish rather than oscillatory. If 0.14 m raises s-bend and slalom progress above iteration 3, the optimum track lies at or above 0.12 m. If it lowers oval progress without helping the s-bend, the tightest bend is limited by turn authority and the track optimum is near 0.12 m.
notes: Single-variable geometry test (wheel_track 0.12 to 0.14 m) from the Builder, with kp raised from 0.8 to 0.93 to hold effective steering gain constant. This follows the iteration 3 baseline (69.18) and the iteration 4 narrow-track result (53.14), which showed that narrowing the track hurts bend progress.
rationale: Evidence: iteration 3 (80 mm row, 0.12 m track, kp 0.8, kd 0.15) is the best so far at 69.18. Max error sits at 0.062 to 0.067 m on every track while RMS stays at 0.019 to 0.033 m, so the failure is a transient peak on bends. Lookahead has now been tested at 40, 60 and 80 mm and is at its contract maximum. Iteration 4 narrowed the track to 0.10 m (with kp lowered to 0.7) and scored 53.14. Its oval progress fell from 0.229 to 0.183 and s-bend progress from 0.156 to 0.081, while s-bend steering oscillation fell to 0.067. That points to sluggish, under-damped bends rather than jitter. The Builder's proposal widens wheel_track to 0.14 m with all else unchanged. Turn rate per unit wheel difference scales as 1/track, so 0.14 m reduces effective steering gain by about 0.12/0.14 = 0.857. I hold effective gain near the iteration 3 level by raising kp from 0.8 to 0.93 (0.8/0.857, about 16 percent). kd stays at 0.15 and ki at 0, because no steady offset has been seen and the damping question is still open. base_speed (1.5), line_loss (last_direction) and sensor weights are unchanged from the best run. Expected result, not yet measured: a narrower gap in the s-bend and slalom progress relative to 0.12 m, with max error near or below 0.060 m. The main risk is reduced turn authority on the tightest bend, which would show as an oval progress drop.
